title: Overcome Evil With Good
headline: After You Resist: What Is the Christlike Response?
tagline: Victory is not merely refusing the old response. It is learning the Christlike response that belongs in its place.
seo_title: Overcome Evil With Good: Romans 12:21 for Men | TheWrkShop
seo_description: If bitterness leaves, what belongs there? A devotional for men on Romans 12:21 and Ephesians 4:31-32 about kindness, compassion and forgiveness.
verse_text: Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.

scriptures.text: Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.
Get rid of all bitterness, rage and anger, brawling and slander, along with every form of malice. Be kind and compassionate to one another, forgiving each other, just as in Christ God forgave you.
Rather, clothe yourselves with the Lord Jesus Christ….

items: When we take spiritual formation seriously, we become very good at identifying what is wrong.
I shouldn’t be bitter.
I shouldn’t compare.
I shouldn’t control.
I shouldn’t retaliate.
All true.

blocks.text: But eventually we have to ask:

items: If bitterness leaves, what belongs there?
If fear stops governing, what takes its place?
If people-pleasing is surrendered, how do I now love people?
If retaliation is surrendered, how do I respond to the person who hurt me?
The Christian life is not merely becoming skilled at saying no.
It is also learning what Christ calls us to say yes to.

sections.label: Paul Doesn’t Leave the Space Empty

items: Paul says get rid of bitterness, rage, anger, brawling, slander and malice.
Then he immediately gives another way of being:
Be kind.
Be compassionate.
Forgive.
Something is removed.
Something is formed.

blocks.text: “If I didn’t do the wrong thing, I won the battle.”

items: Maybe.
Someone insults you.
You don’t retaliate.
Good.
But you rehearse the insult internally for three days.
There is another level of victory available.
Evil does not get to choose what it produces in you.
Freedom from people-pleasing should make us better at loving people, not worse.
Obedience can begin before the emotion catches up.
Don’t only ask what needs to stop. Ask what Christ intends to form in its place.
